field.name: STEP_TEXT
field.value: <<bb>>Receiving Inspection <</bb>> <<nl/>><<nl/>>PPE: Gloves, Eye <<nl/>>Environment: Receiving <<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>>TWO PEOPLE MUST LIFT THE PART OUT OF THE CARRIER. Parts should always be handled wearing gloves. Parts should be carefully removed from there packaging. Utilize caution the Bell Jar is very heavy and very fragile, Also look for the Tube Injectors, they are usually packaged together, and can fall out of the bag and be damaged. A thorough inspection will determine the general condition of all the parts. Check the Bell Jar and Injector tube kit for any chips, cracks, or hairline fractures, also inspect the Bell Jar O-ring surface for any deep scratches. FYI there may be some residual process cooling water still in the cooling jacket, this is usually inert, however still conduct a PH test prior to proceeding. Notify the Production Manager, or Shift Supervisor of any discrepancies.

field.name: STEP_TEXT
field.value: <<bb>>Disassemble <</bb>> <<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>>To protect the Vacuum Seal of the Bell Jar place two layers of masking tape on the O-ring sealing surface, then trim off the excess. Blow out any residual process cooling water from the copper coil with CDA, then wrap the ends of copper coil with masking tape. This will prevent beads from either entering the coil or damaging the threads of the fittings. Your now ready for bead blasting.Mask the sealing surface, the cooling tubes and any metal on the outside of the bell jar with at least 2 layers of tape before proceeding to the production area.
